factors.factor: The IPC Template Type definition declared 21 expected inputs, but the sensor code supplied only 20 input values to the Content Interpreter; this inconsistency between definition and implementation was not reconciled or detected before release.
factors.evidence: "The definition of the IPC Template Type in the Template Type Definitions file stated that it expected 21 input fields. The sensor code that invoked the Content Interpreter with Channel File 291's Template Instances supplied only 20 input values to match against."

factors.factor: Testing was focused on functional validation and did not exercise the 21st input field with realistic or non-wildcard criteria, so the mismatch went undetected.
factors.evidence: "Manual and automated testing were performed during development, focused on functional validation"; "a static set of 12 test cases was selected... used a regex wildcard matching criterion in the 21st field for all Template Instances." | "The IPC Template Type was stress tested with a test Template Instance... It passed the stress test and was validated for use." | "No IPC Template Instances in previous channel file versions had used the 21st input parameter field."

factors.factor: The Content Validator checked channel files against the expected 21-input definition rather than against what the sensor code actually supplies, so it passed content that would crash sensors.
factors.evidence: "The Content Validator evaluated the new Template Instances. It based its assessment on the expectation that the IPC Template Type would be provided with 21 inputs."

factors.factor: The sensor's Content Interpreter code did not bounds-check input array access: it performed a NULL pointer check, then read through an invalid pointer at index 0x14 (the 21st element of a 20-element array), and because the code ran in a kernel driver, the fault produced a system-wide bugcheck.
factors.evidence: "The code read the input at index 0x14 (the 21st element), which did not point to valid memory. The code performed a NULL pointer check, then read through the invalid pointer, resulting in the out-of-bounds read and the bugcheck."

action_items.action: Reconcile the IPC Template Type definition (21 expected inputs) with the sensor code that supplies inputs (20 values), and add a build-time or CI check that fails when the number of inputs declared in the Template Type Definitions file does not match the number supplied by the sensor code.

Modify the Content Validator to validate channel files against the input arity the sensor actually supplies at runtime, rather than only the declared definition, and reject Template Instances that reference input indices beyond that arity.

Harden the Content Interpreter so that every input index access is bounds-checked against the actual array length, and treat missing or out-of-range inputs as a safe no-match rather than dereferencing them; correct the NULL-check-then-read pattern so that an invalid pointer is never dereferenced.

Extend the test corpus for Template Types to exercise every declared input field with realistic and non-wildcard criteria, and add fuzz and stress tests that generate Template Instances across the full range of input arities and matching criteria, including ones using previously unused fields.
